product_scope: itpay is the single public CLI entry point, and $itpay is its user-facing Skill invocation. Under that one product entry point, the two top-level commerce actions are buy and sell: Buyer workflows are available now; Seller workflows use the same entry point via itpay sell.
title: Railway Query, Planning, and Ticket Booking
purpose: One railway route from understanding the request to saved results, booking, protected checkout, order status and refunds.
when_to_use: Any railway schedule, planning or ticket request; read this topic once before the first railway action.

goal_and_overview.route: Understand constraints → form a credible station-pair hypothesis → choose Exact or Smart → read saved results and select → create booking → obtain only missing human consent → show official entry → read the same order state.
goal_and_overview.query_vs_booking: Exact/Smart returns a query execution and saved evidence. Booking creates a separate execution from a server-issued selection; it is not a repeated search.
goal_and_overview.comparison: If the human only asked to compare, answer from the results and stop. A clear purchase delegation permits selection under their rules, subject to required human terms.

flow_at_a_glance.returns: one station-pair query execution, resolved scope and either useful results or a same-execution wait action
flow_at_a_glance.next: follow the current next command when still working; compare results and stop if the request is satisfied

flow_at_a_glance.returns: one broader planning execution, observed coverage and either useful results or a same-execution wait action
flow_at_a_glance.next: follow the current next command when still working; compare results and stop if the request is satisfied

flow_at_a_glance.returns: saved rows with a stable detail.command for each train or journey
flow_at_a_glance.next: for a delegated purchase, run the chosen row's detail.command; do not resubmit the query

flow_at_a_glance.returns: a separate booking execution using the returned selection token, seat code and party size
flow_at_a_glance.next: follow its review or waiting action on that same booking execution

flow_at_a_glance.returns: current review revision, material terms and a non-executable confirm_booking input_template
flow_at_a_glance.next: submit the returned actor-type human template only after genuine consent; reuse an unchanged explicit consent for code-only correction

flow_at_a_glance.command: use the returned next or handoff for the same booking execution
flow_at_a_glance.next: do not infer paid or issued from the handoff
use orders-refunds for the same order when needed

understand_before_search: Identify date, arrival deadline, party size, destination precision, speed versus broad coverage, and whether the human delegated buying.

Use existing knowledge or one brief official information lookup to form a credible station pair. It helps identify stations, not current trains, seats, prices or global optimality. Do not make external research mandatory.

For Shanghai to Changsha with a fast arrival before 15:00, Shanghai Hongqiao → Changsha South is a credible pair to verify first with Exact. State the intended scope in one sentence; do not re-ask the stated speed preference.
A city or district is an area, not necessarily the namesake station. Shanghai station and Shanghai city can look similar in text but have different scope.

choose_search.exact: Known or credible resolved station pair, direct trains for one station pair and date only. A zero result does not mean the whole city has no train. Another evidence-based pair may be checked under the original request.
choose_search.smart: Broad station comparison, transfers, uncertain places, or a concrete address with ground connections. Fastest does not automatically mean max_transfers=0.
choose_search.scope: Exact cannot claim a citywide or all-transfer optimum. Smart gives its observed scope and missing evidence; its first useful options may be shown before expansion finishes.

exact.contract: Only origin, destination and travel_date are accepted. Use station names, not an undocumented station-code field. Filter time, seat and quantity against returned rows. Date is illustrative; use the actual requested queryable date.

smart.contract: Origin/destination may be areas or precise places. Adult passengers is an integer 1–5. arrive_before maps to arrive_by; conflicting aliases are rejected. preference_context is currently unsupported; do not send it.

input_and_expected_result.result: Read the resolved station pair or area scope, observed coverage, complete compact train rows, fare/inventory evidence and stable references. The recommendation card is not the full catalog. Unknown cost and unverified address ground facts remain unknown.
input_and_expected_result.waiting: A query run waits within a bound. To continue, use the same execution with itpay services next <execution_id> --timeout 120 --json; it is read-only. Do not sleep/get/events repeatedly or resubmit input.
input_and_expected_result.followup: Read the saved result for the original execution. Smart: itpay services read-result <execution_id> --snapshot <snapshot_id> --json. Exact: use its returned saved-result reader. Filter all existing rows before considering a new supplier query. Planning deadline does not erase saved facts; an old selection token is not refreshed by rereading.

select_and_book.delegation: If the human delegated selection under clear rules, filter all eligible rows and pick accordingly. If no choice matches, report what was checked without loosening constraints. Never present a station-pair result as a global optimum.
select_and_book.input: Use the returned booking_template selection token, passenger count and a seat_type code matched to seat_name (for example O may mean 二等座 in that returned offer). Never send the display name as the code or guess a code for another train.
select_and_book.single_leg: Booking accepts one leg. Smart transfer options require separate leg purchases without a joint seat or connection guarantee; do not send a multi-leg basket.
select_and_book.identity: Passenger name, ID and phone are entered on the official protected checkout page, not in query or booking JSON.

review_and_checkout.review: Read the current booking review revision, actual train/date/stations, seat code and name, party, price state and notice terms. Submit workflow:confirm_booking with actor-type human only after real human consent to required terms, including seat assignment not guaranteed. Do not forge a human actor from agent delegation.
review_and_checkout.equivalent_correction: If only seat code spelling changes while train, actual seat class, party, price and terms are identical, reuse an existing explicit human approval. Material draft changes or missing approval require human confirmation.
review_and_checkout.checkout: Show the returned safe itinerary summary and official link/QR supported by the actual host. Do not repeat a price approval already valid for unchanged terms. The human completes identity and payment on that page. Handoff is not payment or ticket issuance.

continue_and_aftercare.same_execution: Wait and read the same query or booking execution. Once an order exists, use itpay order <order_id> --json for its authoritative state. Paid can still be issuing; report issued only when confirmed.
continue_and_aftercare.saved_vs_live: A saved snapshot remains historical evidence after expiry. Real-time booking or quote credentials may expire and require the documented fresh validation path; rereading an old token does not renew it.
continue_and_aftercare.refund: Read itpay docs show orders-refunds --json and the current order policy. Railway supplier cancellation/return and platform refund have separate facts; a refund request is not completed railway return.

exceptional_branches.login_required: Use itpay auth login --json, complete the official handoff, then execute the returned recovery command for the same paused query. Login returning a command does not execute it.
exceptional_branches.rate_limited: Respect returned retry_after and continue the same execution.
exceptional_branches.booking_review_invalid: Read the same booking review and use the returned seat code; reuse real consent only under the strict equivalent-correction rule.
exceptional_branches.booking_review_changed: Read the current revision and compare material terms; confirm new terms only when changed.
exceptional_branches.selection_stale: Saved result stays readable, but follow the current owner action for new live inventory and quote evidence; do not assume reread refreshes the token.
exceptional_branches.unknown_paid_outcome: Read the same checkout/order before any mutation. Never repeat payment or create a new order on an unknown outcome.
exceptional_branches.lock: Use the CLI returned device repair-lock recovery only for a lock proven stale; preserve active owners and identity.
exceptional_branches.empty: Report verified scope, failures and missing evidence separately. Do not guess a new date or station as a generic repair.
exceptional_branches.ground_evidence_required: If trains were found but a precise address deadline cannot be verified without ground or station-exit evidence, report the checked rail scope and missing fact. Ask for a precise location or verifiable connection fact; do not expand rail station pairs by default or call it no trains.

seat_preferences.meaning: A buyer's seat-letter preference may be planned per leg before payment. The plan is submitted to the supplier when encodable; unsupported combinations fall back to automatic assignment.
seat_preferences.letters: Evidence-backed letters only: O=ABCDF (second class), M=ACDF (first class), 9=ACF (business class). Other layouts auto-assign.
seat_preferences.boundary: Never claim a preference was fulfilled before supplier confirmation; check the issued seat in the order/status output.
seat_preferences.review_contract: Submitted inside the confirm_booking action via --input-json (nested JSON; --input key=value cannot express it and must not be combined with it). One preference per passenger slot, passenger_index 0-based. draft_revision must equal the server projection; a stale revision returns booking_review_changed — re-read services next and resubmit, never increment locally.
seat_preferences.revision: While payment has not started, the same execution accepts a revised review: resubmit confirm_booking with the new draft_revision; the old unpaid quote/checkout is retired and re-quoted. After a payment attempt the review is closed — never create a replacement purchase.

notifications.channels: Delivery notices reach the checkout-confirmed contact: email always works; a verified mainland SMS recipient is optional and checkout-scoped. The passenger phone, the login phone and the notification recipient are independent facts.
notifications.status_read: The order read exposes masked per-leg notification entries (keys: issued, details_pending, seat_ready) with channel, status and masked recipient — never raw numbers.
notifications.truthfulness: Provider acceptance is not delivery; an uncertain send outcome is reconciled, not silently retried. A notification failure never changes ticket or refund state; report it as a delivery detail, not an order failure.
notifications.unavailable: If SMS is not configured or a recipient is unverified, email still satisfies the contact policy — never present an unverified phone as enabled.
